utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Would you like to continue with witness L? We are still in closed session. WITNESS L, recalled Examined by MR. NIEMANN, continued.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Witness L, you understand that you are still under the oath that you took yesterday to tell the truth? You understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Niemann.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Witness, do you recall yesterday afternoon just prior to the adjournment we were talking about events that were happening on 5th November 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you recall in the early afternoon of that day three men being taken out of the co-operative building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again may I raise a matter here, your Honour, about the leading of my learned friend in relation to this witness?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, it is leading. Do you recall a matter relating to the three men being taken out of the co-operative building? That is a new issue. You are not talking about the same one?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour. I have to take the witness to the incident.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is this a new incident or is this the one, the elderly men, I thought that was four men.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, this is a new incident, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You do not think that is leading?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Not to introduce a new incident, your Honour. Once I have identified the incident for the witness and the witness can come on, certainly I accept that, but the witness ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. It is probably preliminary. I think it is preliminary. Once he gets into it, he is introducing and it is preliminary. So, I will not overrule. I will overrule the objection, will not sustain the objection, but when you get beyond the preliminary matters, then be careful not to lead the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you want to repeat that preliminary question?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, the witness says he recalls it.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see who it was that was leading these three men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember there was Bosko Dragicevic, Zoran Karajica and Milan Cavic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where had they taken the men from, could you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took them out from dom, and took them towards the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did anyone else then arrive on the scene?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was Dragicevic, there was Dusko Tadic at the time. He returned in his car.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did Dusko Tadic stay on the scene or did he leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He left.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did the men then do with the three prisoners that were being taken out of the co-operative building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took them to the white house which can be seen from my guard post and harassed them there, beat them, and then they were followed by Bosko Dragicevic as Dusko Tadic went towards Kozarac in his car, but Dragicevic came back and went to the white house and bid me -- sorry, came to me and then told me to come along, to come with him, because there was a task I had to perform. I asked him how could I leave my sentry post, and he told me that I could do that because Sinisa Popovic would cover it. As we went out of the camp, he took my rifle away from me and we passed by the command, by the headquarters, which is on the right side of the road. We went past that and reached the white house. That white house is on the -- to the right from the elementary school from the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did Dragicevic tell you what it was that he wanted you to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He told me that there was a task there, that there were some three old men and that I was to fire several bullets into them. They were quite old.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did you say to him when he told you this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said I did not want to do it and let them do it, and he threatened that he would kill me unless I did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you arrived at the white house, can you describe the way the three men prisoners were being retained at the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we reached that white house, there was a post -- there was a bar next to the house and there were two posts about two, 2.5 metres tall.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know what this bar and two posts had been used for prior to this day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that bar served, it was an unfinished house, and it was used to help put the building materials up in building.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was it a sort of scaffolding, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, I did not hear the question quite well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was it some form of scaffolding for working on the building for people to stand on when they work on the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was this post with the horizontal bar being used for when you arrived at the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean with that horizontal bar, sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, what were they doing with it on that day, the day you got there, on that day that the three men were taken there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was some 15 metres away from it. Those old men were beaten. They were tied to that bar, that is, their hands, their hands were, and with spread arms they were tied up to this horizontal bar, and after sometime they move away and I was ordered to kill those old men.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who gave you that order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bosko Dragicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you immediately comply with the order or did you hesitate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I did comply with the orders immediately. I was standing and asked him why was I to kill those people, what was the reason for it because they had done no wrong to me, to kill anyone, it was the first time I was to kill someone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did Dragicevic then do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They told me I had to or else he would kill me. I was under a threat and after some time I had to fire into those inmates.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What part of their bodies did you fire into?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The area of chest, head.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: About how many bullets did you fire into the three men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I fired some 15 bullets.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you describe the scene there when you had finished firing the 15 bullets at the three old men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, where was that house?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, no. What did you see after you had immediately fired the bullets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, I did not quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I will move on. What happened next? What was the next thing to happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: People were slain and meanwhile Zoran Karajica arrived with a small TAM, blue, and those prisoners were taken off the bar and then we loaded them on to that blue little TAM, and we started to a dump site,

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted) and there we came to a halt, parked, dragged those three corpses from the truck and dumped them on to that dump site.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: As you were unloading these corpses, did you notice anything about the dump site?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as I was standing on that dump site I saw human skulls, bones, very many cadavers, human, and there was stench.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You said a little while ago that it was a little blue TAM, you mean a little blue TAM truck, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After you unloaded the corpses at this dump site, did you then return to your guard post?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did you feel like when you returned to your guard post?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I felt sick. I was not feeling well. I threw up. I felt very sick.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you then see Dragicevic shortly after this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dragicevic brought me a box of ammunition which I fired into those three corpses. Those were about 15 bullets. I was at the guard post where there was this small structure. I was sitting. He gave me this ammunition and he realised that I was feeling poor and asking for a doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened then? What was the next thing to happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He summoned a doctor and after a while a Dr. Baja came and Dr. Nevenka, and he called me from my sentry post to come into the office and there I was given an injection.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What effect did this injection have upon you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I felt very strong after some 10 minutes. I did not, I was not quite conscious, not -- excuse me, not that I was totally unconscious, but I did not feel, I began to feel very strong, very powerful and I felt quite differently after that injection.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Prior to this day, had you ever taken drugs, had you ever taken drugs that made you feel this particular way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some pills and some syrup I would drink with those pills.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: But had you ever taken drugs that gave this sort of reaction to you before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean before?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: About dusk on the same day, that is, 5th November 1992, did you see another girl led out of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. A girl was taken out then.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see who it was that took her out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember, but there were Bosko Dragicevic, Zoran Karajica, Milan Cavic and Dusko Tadic were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see where this girl was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The girl was taken from the primary school and taken into the cellar of the white house where they generally committed murders and rapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you go with them on this occasion or did you stay behind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went with them. They called me to come along.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you went into the basement who did you see there in the basement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a girl, Zoran Karajica, Milan Cavic and there was Dusko Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you remember about how old this girl looked to be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That girl was about 17 or 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you remember whether she was a tall person or a short person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She was rather tall, fair, thin.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you remember any of the clothes that she had on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, she had trousers, black with a black belt, and a sports jacket, black shoes and white stockings -- white socks, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you went into the basement, when you first went into the basement, what was the girl doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She was struggling. She was trying to defend herself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What were the men doing to the girl, could you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were dealing her blows, slapping her face, so that she would stop wrestling away and there was Dusko Tadic who threatened that he would kill her and slit her throat, and she heard that and she was more pleading for help.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did they then do to the girl?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They stripped her naked and pushed her down on to the mattress. Her eyes were blindfolded, but she was wrestling and then fighting, and after a while Dusko Tadic took out a police baton. He was tapping it on the palm of his hand and the girl was trying to wrestle away and crying and begging, and then Dusko Tadic put the baton into her mouth.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then I was ordered to undress and then to perform rape.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you do this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you think this girl was a virgin or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She was, because as I was entering her I penetrated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did anyone do anything to you while you were raping this girl?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bosko Dragicevic was pushing me down, I cannot remember whether with his foot or a baton, on my back and as I was penetrating the girl and he did not allow me until I finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After you had raped the girl, what did you then do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I got off the girl and I put on my clothes and after that Dusko (sic) Dragicevic took off his belt and he had a pistol and a baton on it, and then he started. I wanted to take this pistol from him with the belt, but he did not allow me to take it, and rather gave it to Dusko Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I just wish to mention something about the transcript. You say "Dusko Dragicevic", did you understand his first name to be "Dusko"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Bosko Dragicevic. I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that Dragicevic then started, did he then start to rape the girl?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When Dragicevic was raping the girl, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was holding one leg of this girl, as far as I remember, and after that the girl was raped by Dragicevic and then he got off her and then they ordered her to put her clothes on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You said a moment ago in your evidence that you went to take the pistol of Dragicevic but you were not allowed to take it. Do you know why this was, they did not let you take it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that they thought that I would kill somebody there. When I went from my guard post he took my rifle away from me, because I would not allow somebody to do something. It was very difficult for me and terrible to what he was making me do as well as others, but I was under the orders to do something.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: On the way back to the camp did they speak to this girl?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not, but Dusko Tadic and the other policemen were threatening her that she -- that nobody in the camp must know what happened to her.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: On the next day, that is 6th November, did you go to work at the camp on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you ask Bosko Dragicevic if you could have the day off?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Why did you ask for the day off?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because my mother was ill and I also had a small sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did Dragicevic say to you when you asked him to take the day off?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He told me that I could not get that day off, but I could get the next day off because there was going to be a check up in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say a "check up", do you mean medical check up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a medical check up.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Later on that day or that morning was there a medical check up carried on of the guards of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a check up of all the guards and I also got an injection, and after a while this Dr. Baja and the nurse, Nevenka, were in the camp with all the inmates who were in the camp, in the school and the co-operative, and after a while they came out and they left towards Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you receive an injection this day similar to the one you had received on the previous day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did it have a similar effect upon you to the injection that you had on the previous day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Around noon on that day, did you see another girl being led out of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know where she was being led from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That girl was taken out of the school building and her hands were tied behind her back. As far as I remember, there were Bosko Dragicevic, Zoran Karajica and Cavic. They took the girl towards the white house. After a while Dragicevic called me to come with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you then go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you got to the white house did you go into the basement again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened then when you went into the basement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were taking the clothes off of this girl and they stripped her naked. Then they pushed her down on to the mattress.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you recall, approximately, how old this girl was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That girl had about 20 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First, they pushed the girl down on to the mattress and then Zoran Karajica took his clothes off, lay down on the girl to commit the rape and then he performed the rape. After him, they forced me to perform rape of this girl.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was this girl upset and crying when this was all happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, she was trying to break away. She was trying to defend herself, and she was looking for the worst.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know a person at the camp, a guard at the camp, by the name of Baltic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dragan?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was he at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: About how old was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was about 40 to 45.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know where he came from, what area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was from Prijedor, towards Prijedor, but that was Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: On the day that this girl was raped, the one you just spoke of, did you see Dragan Baltic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was also there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see him do anything to the girl?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After my rape of this girl, he took off his clothes and straddled the girl and then he came on her breasts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After this girl was raped where did you go then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We returned to the camp. They returned the girl to the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In the afternoon of the same day, 6th November 1992, did you again see two elderly prisoners being led from the co-operative building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, the question was a little -- was asked a bit differently with Mr. Niemann.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I will ask the question again. In the afternoon of the same day, 6th November 1992, did you see two elderly prisoners being led from the co-operative building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as they were being led from the co-operative building, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see who it was that was leading these men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure who took them out, but Zoran Karajica and Cavic and Bosko Dragicevic were present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know in what direction they were leading these men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those people were taken out of the co-operative and they led them past command. There was a building where it was the headquarters for Dragicevic and Dusko Tadic. Then they led the men past that command building headquarters and to the white house which could be seen from my guard post. They brought them to this white house and they were being beaten with batons. They were being beaten. Dragicevic called me to come with him, and in that -- at that time he also took the rifle off my shoulder and he was carrying it. As we arrived to the white house, the two prisoners were tied up to the pole and then I received the order to kill those two old men.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The pole they were tied up to, is this the same pole as the other men had been tied up to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you obey the order to kill these men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you fire at these men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What parts of their bodies did you strike with your bullets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I was about 15 metres away as Zoran Karajica came from behind to me, and he took the rifle and folded the stock. It is a rifle. It is an automatic rifle that has stock, that means to be folded. Then he cocked it for me and he held my arm and leaned it against my shoulder and ordered me, and he showed me to shoot in the region of the head, of the forehead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you do this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After you had shot them in the region of the head, what did you then do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I killed those inmates, and after that we returned to the camp. Those corpses remained on that pole. I do not know what happened to them, where they were dragged or where they were dumped and who took them off.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: On the next day, 7th November 1992, did you again go and see Dr. Baja?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Why did you go and see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was receiving injections. I needed the injections.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you beginning to depend upon these injections?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did they help you cope with what you were doing at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, quite a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Why did you have an injection first thing when you got to work on that day? Why did you have the injection then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Why did you feel that you needed the injection on that day when you arrived at work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew that there was going to be some -- either some murdering or some taking out of girls to be raped.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Shortly after you took up position at your guard post, did you see two girls being led out of the school building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see who it was that led the girls out of the school building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Present were Zoran Karajica, Cavic Dragicevic. After a while Dusko Tadic arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened then? What was the next thing to happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took out two girls from the school, and then took them out of the camp. They took them past the offices and they took them to the white house. Dragicevic called me to come with him. We went past the white house and we arrived to a shed which was not far from the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you with them when they arrived at the shed, with these men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, with the girls. I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes. Can you describe the shed? What was it made of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That shed was made of concrete blocks, called Siporeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did it have windows and doors?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was inside the shed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a mattress and some wood, some logs of wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you went into this shed, what did they do to the girls?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The girls were untied, their hands were untied, and Dusko Tadic ordered them to undress, that we were not going to undress them because they were dirty and they cried and they begged them not to do this. They had to undress naked and the first girl was pushed down on to the mattress and the second girl was ordered to sit on her face.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the first girl was lying down on the mattress and the other girl was lying on her face, then Dusko Tadic undressed and lay down on the girl and performed the rape.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: While Tadic was raping the girl, what were the other men doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were holding the first girl who was raped by Tadic and the other girl who was sitting on her face as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After Tadic had raped the girl, what was the next thing to happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They lifted the girl, the first, the girl that was sitting on her face, then they lifted the girl that was raped by Tadic, and then there were two girls so it is more difficult to describe. They pushed down the second girl and they ordered me to rape her.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you comply with that order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you ejaculate inside the girl?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: While you were raping this girl, what were the others doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were holding that girl that was raped by Tadic and this girl that I was raping, and they were laughing from what I was doing, what I was doing with the girl.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After the two girls had been raped, what was the next thing to happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The girls, after they were raped, they were ordered to dress. Then they got dressed and Tadic ordered them to beat each other because of some gold, because the girls were threatened that they did, did not -- were told not to let anybody know in the camp and that they were also beating each other over some gold for about some 10 minutes. Then Tadic separated them and they were laughing and saying how Balinkas are hating each other because they were beating each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Tadic ordered them to fight?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was there any gold there at all or was this an imaginary fight about gold?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not gold. That was imaginary. It is not imaginary -- that is what they were ordered because they were raped, those girls, so that the other inmates in the camp would not know what happened to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: They were told not to mention the fact that they had been raped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After these girls had been raped and after the fight, what happened? What was the next thing that happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were returned to the camp, to the school building.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you go back to your guard post?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Later on on the same day, 7th November 1992, was another girl led out of the school building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you remember about what time of the day this was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall exactly, but it was after those girls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Could you see or did you see who it was that led these girls out of the school building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were Zoran Karajica, Cavic Dragicevic and Baltic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Could you see about how old this girl was, were you able to estimate that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The girl was around 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In which direction did they start to take the girl?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took her out of the school and then they brought her to the white house and they took her down to the basement of the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you with them on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who told you to join them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dragicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was the lighting like when you arrived at this place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, as far as I recall, it was pretty dark in that basement, otherwise they were bringing lights with them, so there was a lamp that was lit there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The lamp that was lit, was this like a lantern, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened when you arrived at this place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They stripped the girl completely naked, and they pushed her down on to the mattress and she tried to break away and she tried to defend herself. Bosko Dragicevic performed the rape of that girl.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After Dragicevic had raped the girl, what was the next thing to happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dragicevic raped that girl and then stood up, and then I was ordered to take my clothes off and also to perform the rape of that girl.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After the girl was raped, what happened next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She was returned to the camp. She was also threatened that she would be killed if people in the camp learned what had happened to her.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Two or three days after this incident, on or about 9th or 10th November 1992, did you see two men being taken from the co-operative building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two prisoners were taken out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you remember who it was that took them out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bosko Dragicevic and Baltic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were they being restrained in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Their hands were tied on the back. They were led out of the co-operative, taken to the white house and they were also beaten and harassed. They reached that white house and then they were tied to the bar and Dragicevic bid me to come along. So I walked to the white house with him and then he ordered me to commit the murder of those two prisoners, to kill them. I did not want to do it, but I was under a threat that I had to do it. I performed the murder of those two prisoners. Dragicevic ordered me to untie them from the bar. I did. They fell down on the ground (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I reached that site, I saw very many bones and skulls and human corpses. I realised that very many corpses had been thrown in there. (redacted) (redacted) Dragicevic had threatened me not to talk about what I had seen at that dump site, what was there, and I was under a threat.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you then return to your post?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Some days later, on about 15th November 1992, did you see seven elderly men being taken out of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You have mentioned in evidence so far about Zoran Karajica. Do you know whether or not he had a brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Zeljko.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: About how old was Zeljko, can you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot really remember but he was older than I.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you think he was in his 20s, 30s or 40s? Can you assist us in that way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember. He was young, slightly older than I.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who did you see lead the seven men out of the camp on this day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zoran Karajica, Cavic, Zeljko Karajica -- they are brothers -- Bosko Dragicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In what direction were they leading these men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They led those seven prisoners out of the co-operative, took them towards the white house and they had their hands tied on their backs. They were brought to that white house and they harassed them and beat them, those prisoners. They brought them to that white house. I was on duty at my sentry post and was observing what was happening. They brought them to the white house and there they tied them up to that bar. In the meantime, Dragicevic returned, got a rifle from the office and went to that white house and then they performed murders. As far as I can remember, Dragicevic was the first one to fire. Then he turned the rifle over to other policemen and then they fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After they fired on these seven elderly men, did you see what they did with their bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took them off that bar. Zoran Karajica, the one who had the small blue TAM, brought it along so they piled those corpses on to a truck, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: On the same day did you see another girl being led from the elementary school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you remember who it was that led this girl out of the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it was Dragicevic, Zoran Karajica and Cavic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was this girl being restrained or tied up in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they led her out of the school, they tied her hands at the back and then they brought her out of the school and went past the co-operative to the exit gate and took her past the office and they took her to the cellar, to the basement, of the white house. Dragicevic bid me to come along. I left my sentry post and I came with him, but he took my rifle off my shoulder and left it in his office.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you able to estimate, approximately, how old this girl was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That girl was about 17 or 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you recall the colour and style, the way she had her hair made up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She had long hair, plaited, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you got into the basement what did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we entered it, they were stripping the girl and they stripped her naked, pushed her down on to the mattress and then ordered me to perform the rape of this girl.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you rape the girl?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was this girl distressed at the time this was all happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did they say anything to the girl?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They told her that no girl would leave the camp without and not be pregnant.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After this rape did you then go back to your guard post?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In the afternoon of the same day, did you see them take out another girl from the elementary school building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see who it was that took this girl out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were also Dragicevic, Zoran Karajica, Cavic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you remember what the colour of the girl's hair was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember from before, it is three years since, the girl had fair hair, curly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did they take this girl to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also took her out of the school and they took her passed, took her out from the camp grounds and took her to the cellar, to the basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: As they took the girl out of the school, were you spoken to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dragicevic told me to come with him. I left the sentry post. I came with him. We reached that white house. We entered the basement. The girl was undressed, pushed down on to the mattress. The girl was trying to break away from them and was crying and Dragicevic said he would rape her first because she was fighting and crying. So Dragicevic performed the rape of that girl. Then they forced me to also perform the rape of that girl.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you rape the girl?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did anyone other than you and Dragicevic rape this girl, that you can remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After the girl had been raped, was she then led back to the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you again return to your guard post?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Several days later, on about 18th November 1992, did you see six prisoners being taken out of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you remember about what time of the day this was when they were taken out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was, perhaps, somewhere around noon or in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see who it was that led them out of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I recall, it was Dragicevic, Zoran Karajica, Cavic and after a certain time Dragan Maric.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did they take these six men to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took them out of the co-operative and to the white house where they performed murders before.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: This person you have mentioned, Dragan Maric, did you know of him from the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you tell us, approximately, what age he was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Roughly my age, born in '75 perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know where he came from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From my area, the one that I fled, that I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did they do with Dragan Maric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He went with those prisoners and, as far as I remember, he performed the killing of those six prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: As he was being led towards the white house, did they do anything with his rifle, can you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After these six men had been killed, did you see what they did to the corpses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were taken away, that blue TAM which Zoran Karajica had. They were taken to a dump site.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you stay at your guard post right throughout this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Could you have a clear view of what you saw happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: One morning around 25th November 1992, do you recall seeing 10 elderly prisoners being led out of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When they took these men out of the camp, what did they then do to them or with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those people were taken out of the co-operative. Their hands were tied at the back. Meanwhile, Dusko Tadic had arrived. They led those prisoners out on to the asphalt. They were shoved on to a truck, on to a van. We -- and they started towards the railway station, Omarska, and they brought them to the white house and Dusko Tadic was there too and Dragicevic bid me to come with him. He took the rifle off my shoulder. We walked past the office and reached that white house. Those prisoners had already been tied to the bar and they were also harassed. Tadic then turned to me -- well, no, he did not address me. He said, "Guy, come here to perform the killing of these 10 prisoners, to kill them", and I said, "Why me? Why do I have to do it?" He said nothing in reply. One of those prisoners heard him order me to kill them, heard Tadic order me that. He then spoke to Tadic and said why is he killing them since they had given him money and gold. Tadic said nothing. He was watching me. Then he approached two of those two prisoners, took out a pistol from the holster and killed those two prisoners right into the head. Then he came to me and ordered me to kill the remaining eight. I was terrified because I knew that Dusko Tadic was the Commander of the camp. I was standing and Zoran Karajica, Dragicevic and Cavic approached, and Zoran Karajica came from behind and stole the rifle off my back and they ordered me that I had to kill the remaining eight. Then I complied with the order and I had to kill those eight. I fired 10 bullets, and I was firing at those two whom Tadic had held and I was ordered to fire off the remaining 20 bullets, that is, to fire two more bullets at each of those bodies. I emptied the cartridge and Zoran Karajica came with a little TAM and they took off those corpses, those 10 from the bar, and shoved them on to the truck, on to the TAM. They were covered with some kind of canvas. Then Dusko Tadic went to the car and started for Kozarac and left in the direction of Omarska. Then we -- I went with Zoran Karajica and Cavic in that little TAM. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted), we arrived there and also awaited Dusko Tadic who was not there. After some time Dusko Tadic drove in with a man, I believe his name was "Dedo". That is how he addressed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: (redacted), was that like a front end loader type earth moving machine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did the driver of that vehicle arrive in a car with Dusko Tadic separately from yourselves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did the driver of this earth moving machine do once he arrived at the scene?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He boarded it and then started digging a hole. As he started digging the hole, and I was standing nearby, and I could see that he was bringing out lots of bones, human bones, skulls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you describe the smell when this happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the stench was very, was very overwhelming. This earth mover, then when after it completed this pit, it drew those bodies into that pit and then started covering it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So the bodies that you had brought there on the TAM truck were then loaded into the hole that the earth moving machine had dug?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you then head back in the TAM truck to Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: On the way back to the camp, did you ask someone about the grave that you had seen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I asked Zoran Karajica whence all those human bones, those skulls dug there next to that dredger, and he told me that they were killed in the area of Kozarac and Trnopolje, people, and that they had been interred there, and that there were about 3,000 thrown into that pit and buried.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: On 27th November 1992, did your mother receive notice that your father had been killed at the front?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was your father brought back and buried on 30th November 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: As a result of this, did you stay away from work for about seven days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: On your first day back at work, around 6th December 1992, did you see two old men being led out of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who led these men out of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were Dragicevic, Zoran Karajica and Cavic, and Dusko Tadic arrived. They led those two prisoners out of the school -- no, excuse me, out of the co-operative -- I am slightly confused -- from the co-operative. They took them along the road which leads towards Kozarac. They tied those two old men. They took them -- they took them past my sentry post on the road and several buildings away from the headquarters, they took them through an orchard, and brought them next to this white house where there was a fruit orchard. Dragicevic bid me to come with him. He took my rifle from me and I came with him to the white house. We walked along the road towards Kozarac. Then we turned right and reached that orchard.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What state were these old men in? Can you describe their physical appearance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were unkempt, they had long beards, long hair like old people, white.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you arrived at the orchard what did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we arrived in the orchard, those two old men were tied to tree trunks and both their legs and arms. Zoran Karajica and Cavic beat them. They sat on them and beat them. Dusko Tadic was standing a little way away. I and Dragicevic reached that orchard. I was standing near Zoran Karajica as he was sitting on that old man and hitting him with a knife. He was cutting his beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see blood on the faces of the old men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were the old men making any noise at the time when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, because their mouths were tied.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did they have a cloth or something across their face?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Eyes, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, across their mouth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had some rags. They were gagged with some rags or some handkerchiefs or something, and over that their mouths were tied so that they would not scream out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What then happened to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was standing next to Zoran Karajica next to that body -- next to that man, I am sorry. I was standing and then Zoran Karajica caught me by the arm and pulled me down on that man. I fell on him. As I was starting to stand up, and then he ordered me not to stand up, to straddle the man. I was sitting on that man and he offered me the knife. Bosko Dragicevic approached me from behind with a rifle and then he pointed the rifle at my back. Zoran Karajica was holding the head and pressing it down to the ground below the chin, and I was crying and I was trying to break away. I did not want to do it. They ordered me to slit that man's throat. I was saying that I could not do that. All that time Dragicevic was standing behind me with a rifle. Tadic was nearby. I turned to the left and I saw I could do nothing because otherwise I was threatened that I would be killed. I turned left my head and I was looking at the other old man, and Tadic was beating that other old man and turned his head so that he could see how I was butchering that old man. I drew the knife across his head. I discarded the knife and the blood spurted on my uniform. I wanted to stand up from that old man, but they did not allow me until he expired. When he expired, they lifted me off that old man and put me on the other one. I was struggling again, fighting and crying, saying I could not do that. Zoran Karajica took the knife which I had thrown away, wiped it off the beard of that old man, the knife which was bloody. I sat down on the other. Dusko Tadic put his foot on his face, on his temple, and pressed his head against the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: This is the old man, put his foot on the temple of the old man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The first old man that you cut with a knife, it says in the translation you drew the knife across his head. Was it across his head or across his throat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Across his throat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Across his throat.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: With the second old man, once Tadic had put his boot on the head of the old man, what was the next thing to happen? What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zoran Karajica gave me the knife, so as to butcher that old man too. I could not. Dusko Tadic drew out a pistol, pointed it at my head. It was a 7.62 pistol. He pointed it at my head, at my forehead, and told me that I had to do it. Bosko Dragicevic pointed the rifle at my back and then Bosko told him not to kill me, that I would do it at least to prick the man's throat with the knife, and I could do nothing but prick that man's throat with the knife, so I stabbed this knife into his throat.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You stabbed the knife rather than pricked the knife, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After this happened, what happened? What was the next thing to happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I put the knife into that man's throat and then Cavic and Karajica lifted me off that body and I went with Dragicevic to the headquarters, and then he gave me a uniform. Tadic, Karajica and Cavic stayed behind in that orchard and I do not know what happened to those corpses then and what went on. I was given another uniform and I returned to my guard post.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After this incident were you feeling sick?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Dr. Baja came and I was given an injection.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Several days later, around 9th or 10th ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Niemann, we will stand in recess for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, would you continue please, with witness L?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I have asked the witness to be brought in, your Honour. WITNESS L, recalled Examined by MR. NIEMANN, continued.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You may be seated. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Witness, several days later after the last incident, around about 9th or 10th December 1992, did you see 10 men being led out of the co-operative building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you remember about what time of day this was that they were brought out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Somewhere around noon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see who it was that was leading them out of the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was Zoran Karajica, Cavic, Bosko Dragicevic and then Dusko Tadic arrived and Zeljko Karajica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know, approximately, what age group these men were, the 10 men that were taken out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were they elderly men or were they young men? Can you help us that way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were sort of elderly, of 55 to 80 years. Those were the ones that were in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did they do with these old men when they led them out of the co-operative building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were taken out of the co-operative building and taken towards the railway station. The police went along with them and Dusko Tadic also. They came to the intersection that leads towards Prijedor, Omarska and Kozarac. They started towards Omarska. On the asphalt, Dragicevic called me to come along and I came along. He took the rifle off my shoulder. We followed these men, and they led the men by some houses and they took -- where they took tools. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted). Dragicevic and myself arrived after him, after those people arrived (redacted) (redacted) and I was there nearby, and Dusko Tadic ordered them to start digging graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say they took tools, were these shovels that they took?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, shovels.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was it the old men, the 10 old men that took the shovels?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you arrived at this place, what happened after the order was given for them to dig the graves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was standing guard, the guard post which was next to (redacted). I separated from the group. That was my order, to be a guard. The prisoners started digging their graves and after some time they dug them out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After they dug out their graves, what was the next thing to happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then Tadic came close to them and told them to put away the tools and to stand by the graves, and they started tying their hands on their backs. One of them, when he saw that the others were having their hands tied, he dropped the tool and started running away. Then Zoran Karajica saw this, him running away, and he killed him with a short burst of bullets.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When this prisoner ran away and was shot, did someone say something to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then Dusko Tadic approached and said that if that prisoner had run away, who was prevented by Zoran Karajica, that I would have been killed and I said that I did not see him, so I defended myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did one of the prisoners then speak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he said, he asked Tadic why he was killing them, that he would like to know about his son, then he would not regret dying. Tadic replied that he would not find out about his son, that prisoner, that he was going to be killed and that he would not know who killed him -- I am sorry, that refers to his son.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That he would be killed and he would not know who had killed his son?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That his son would not know who killed this prisoner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I see. What was the next thing that happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They tied -- by the way, Tadic hit that one with the rifle butt from behind and the man fell down, and then I was ordered to kill the other nine prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did Dragicevic then give you an order in relation to the killing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did he say to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To approach the remaining prisoners and to shoot at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did he say where you should shoot at them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He told me to shoot in their heads, and I was four to five metres away from them. Those prisoners were spaced six to seven metres apart.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you then carry out the order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After you had killed these prisoners, were you then told to do something?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I killed those prisoners, then after me, Zeljko Karajica was shooting at those corpses and then Dragicevic ordered that those corpses be buried there. As we were burying them, Tadic gave Dragicevic an order to make the graves not visible where those people were being buried.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did they tell you how you were to make the graves not visible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To level them so that it is not seen as a grave and to bring the undergrowth and the berries that were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The berries that were there? Were you to cover them with bushes and grass?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After this happened, did you return to the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Several days later, on 13th or 14th December 1992, did Dragicevic call you into his office and ask you something about your father's death?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did he say to you about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He asked me whether I had found out or heard who killed my father, and I answered that I did not, I had not heard, but I knew that he had died on the frontline.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: On the next day did you see two elderly men being taken out of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: About what time of the day was this that you saw this happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot quite recall, but those two elderly prisoners were taken out. They also took them to that white house. Dragicevic called me and told me that those two prisoners, that their sons had escaped from Kozarac and they were in the frontlines, that they had heard that, that their sons killed my father. But I did not believe that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened then to the old men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then, under the orders of Dragicevic, I committed the murders of those two prisoners. I returned to my guard past and I do not know what happened to them afterwards. They remained on that pole.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Towards the end of December, did you see another elderly man taken out of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see who it was that took this old man out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Dusko Tadic and Bosko Dragicevic, and Dusko Tadic told me that I was guilty because of that first man who started to run away and Zoran Karajica then killed him, that I had to commit -- I had to kill this man. That was the punishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did he say that for merely allowing the old man to escape from the grave site when the 10 old men had dug their grave that you had to carry out this killing as punishment for merely allowing that man to escape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you carry out the order to kill this man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you shoot this man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I shot in the region of the legs. After about three minutes and then Dragicevic ordered me to kill him, and then I shot in the region of his chest.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you ordered to shoot in the region of the legs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the calf.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who told you that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dragicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did he say to you about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To stay on a few minutes after I shot him in the legs, and for about three minutes I did not shoot this man and then he ordered me to shoot him in the chest.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Apart from the rapes that you had participated in outside the camp, do you know whether anybody was raped inside the camp itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There were six girls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where were these girls raped, these six girls?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a house -- there were several buildings on the grounds that were about 100 metres away from the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were these buildings occupied?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were previously but they were destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What sort of buildings were these, what building was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a house. It had a balcony. It was -- it had a top floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where was it in relation to the school? Was it in the front of the school or behind the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Behind the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were these girls all raped together or were they raped separately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were taken out in twos, in three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: On three separate occasions did this happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you remember when it was that the first two girls were raped, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometime in December.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you remember what time of the day it was that this occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the afternoon, two girls were taken out, their hands tied behind their backs and there was Zoran Karajica, Cavic, and Dragicevic and there was also Dusko Tadic there. They brought the girls into the house. They called me in. I entered the house, and I saw one girl completely naked. There was a military type of bed in this house. I do not know who brought this girl that was naked, who brought her to the bed and who tied her hands, but I know that Dusko Tadic committed the rape of that girl and then the order was that I rape this girl that Dusan Tadic raped.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How was she tied up? Can you explain to us how she was tied to the bed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Her hand -- her arms and her legs were tied to the bed posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: While this girl was raped, what happened to the other girl?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Her hands were tied and she was blindfolded and her mouth was gagged, and she was by the bed post.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you remember who it was that raped this girl?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The other girl?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, the other girl.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it was Cavic and Zoran Karajica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were there any instructions given about how people were to leave this house after the rapes had occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Everybody left one by one, and one by one girl was taken out of that house and returned into the school building.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you understand why it was that you left the building in this manner or this way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because there were a lot of prisoners in that school and they could see.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The next day were two more girls taken out from the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who took the girls out on this occasion, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot quite say who took the girls out, but Tadic and myself were raping.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see Tadic rape the girl, one of these girls?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you rape one of the girls?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Several days later, were two more girls taken out of the building and brought to this house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see who was there on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was Dusko Tadic, Zoran Karajica, Zeljko, Cavic and Bosko Dragicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were these girls restrained or tied up in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were tied.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where were they tied?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were tied to the bed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were both these girls raped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who raped the girls on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zeljko Karajica, Dusko Tadic and I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you participate in this rape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were both these girls raped at the same time or at different times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One was in the morning and the other one towards the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you rape both the girls on that day or only one of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One girl.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see whether Tadic raped both the girls on that day or only one of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: By the end of December 1992, had your psychological condition deteriorated to the point that you felt it was necessary to leave the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you ask permission to leave the camp or did you just go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I simply left. I escaped.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you escaped, did you leave the area of opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you find a place where you could hide?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How long did you stay in this place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was there about 10 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: During this time that you were there hiding, did you begin to suffer the effects of not having the drugs that you had been given?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you eventually get over this, the effects of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After that where did you go? I am sorry, I will withdraw that question, your Honour. After you had been hiding in this place, did you return to the opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How long did you stay then in opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About a year and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: During that period of year and a half did you obtain work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you hear whether or not anyone had been searching for you since you left the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Bosko Dragicevic and some policemen were looking for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were they able to find you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: On 12th July 1994, did you then join the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you do your military training?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kalinovik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you just tell us, in very general terms, where that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kalinovik is not far from Sarajevo. One goes through Sokolac, Foca, Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After you had finished your military training, did you then go to the front?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where at the front were you stationed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was at Poljedica, Sljemena, Makva(?).

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you remember what time this was in 1994, what month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was around October.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you were fighting at the front were you injured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How were you injured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was wounded in my right side with a sniper.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you shot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some Bosnian Army fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you were shot were you then captured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
