utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Very well. In relation to the petrol station, are you able to identify any other building nearby where we would be able to pinpoint it?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: There was a saw mill.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is down towards the Prijedor/Banja Luka road, is it not?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You describe the house of Dusko Tadic as having a shop. Can you remember what that shop sold?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: That is where the international -- the humanitarian aid was distributed. There was a cafe in my time while I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There was a cafe. So the shop, you say, is the Red Cross office or a shop for the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: That is where Dusko Tadic was distributing for the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have described this as being a white house, is that not right?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did Dusko Tadic have a wife with him at this house?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I do not know Dusko Tadic's wife, but there was a lady. As far as I know the name, it was Branka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you think that she was his wife?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have you ever described in a statement again to the Sarajevo authorities that he had a wife called Branka?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: It is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have not made a mistake and told them something that is wrong, have you?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No, it is not true that his name -- that her name was Branka. I did not know his wife. I did not know that he had a wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just to ask you this again, was there any document that you kept that recorded you working as a guard at Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: It was registered in the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Which headquarters were they? Where were they? The headquarters at Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you describe what that record was, what particular book or document that was?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Book.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It was a book. Did it contain names of other people within that book?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Of all guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you sign it?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But you saw your name inside that book?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You described starting guard duty at a place called guard post 4. What I would like you to do now is to look at a map here which is court Exhibit 309 and point out to us on this plan where guard post 4 was. What I was intending to do was -- yes -- if you call this Defence 34, D34 and use Prosecution Exhibit 309 for the witness to make a mark.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You want the witness to make a mark on D34 which would be Prosecution 309 without the mark?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. I am using the same material.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That there, witness, is a plan of Trnopolje drawn by a witness earlier in the proceedings. Can you recognise on the right-hand side where it indicates the layout of the school in the camp? If you could answer "yes" or "no"?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you recognise ----

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- where it indicates the dom?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And the road to Kozarac running along the side of the camp?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And the road to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What I would like you to do for us is on that plan that you have there is to mark guard post 4 that you have described. I will provide a pen here.

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I am sorry, I have got one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you could also mark the place that you have called the white house, where that would be found.

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the plan].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you could indicate what you have described as the office of Dusko Tadic and Bosko Dragicevic?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the plan].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you could put a 4 by guard post 4 where you have marked that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: He has already done that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If that can be put on the overhead projector so that we can see it? So in the right-hand corner is guard post 4, is that right?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if you use the indicator to point where you have put that, Mr. Wladimiroff tells me.

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I am sorry, can I show you all three things?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I am going to ask you to do. Point to guard post 4 first.

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the plan].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you next point to the white house?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the plan].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you point to the place where you said the office of Dusko Tadic and Bosko Dragicevic was?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the plan].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Beneath Z and A on the plan, is that right?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: This pump, I do not know what these two squares are for.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you could just keep the pointer on where you say the office was?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the plan].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Is that clear to the Court?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, for the record, the guard post is marked with a No. 4 and then the white house is marked with an X.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Then the office, Dragicevic Bosko's office, is marked with a square.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, that would be a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. We will stand in recess for 20 minutes. We can continue tonight until 6 p.m. if we can move along and perhaps finish with this witness, because we have one more witness, as I understand it, who will take from three to five hours and we would like to finish tomorrow, if at all possible. So we are going to check with the persons who assist us to see if we can sit until 6.00 tonight. We will stand in recess for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will continue until 6 p.m. today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am much obliged, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Witness, I would like you to look at this photograph which I tender as D34 and perhaps if it could be shown to Mr. Niemann after it has been given to Mr. Bos?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am sorry. Witness, can you see that photograph and do you recognise it as showing the school buildings at Trnopolje and the road to Kozarac in the middle of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if the overhead projector could be turned round and the photograph be put on that projector? Can you see a telegraph pole by the pile of logs in front of the school?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would it be right to say that your guard post No. 4 was at the other side of that telegraph pole at the corner of the camp where the fence separated the school from the other buildings?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No. My guard post was above the school in the corner where you can see this house. [The witness indicated on the photograph].

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We need the translation for that of the witness. Would you repeat your response, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My guard post was next to this house which you can see here, in the corner. This is guard post No. 4 next to this asphalt.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again using that pen you have on the desk, could you mark that photograph with an X in the position of the guard post so that it is clear?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Sorry, to take the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, and with the pen on your desk could you put an X or put a 4? Put a 4 where the guard post was.

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I can see it. The indentation will be on the photograph, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Excuse me, I cannot determine it quite normally on this picture otherwise ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would it be right to say the logs were not there when you were on guard duty?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I have offered that as D35 and I now produce it to the Court as D35 Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: D35 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like you now to look at another photograph which I tender as D36. If you could show it to Mr. Niemann? Is that a photograph of the road in Trnopolje up to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Showing on the right-hand side the hedges and trees along the road?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you could put that on the overhead projector, please? What distance was the white house in metres from your guard post No. 4?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: About 150, as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did the white house have a road that was a tarmac road leading to it or was it a pathway that was just a dirt path?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: This was a road which one could use with a slightly better, more powerful vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it a dirt road or a dirt path to the white house?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: There was grass.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: All these houses along this road are white, are they not?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I could not say if they were all white.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where did you get this expression "the white house" from? Was that what the other guards called it?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, because that is where murders were being committed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This house then was 150 metres away from your post on the edge of the camp, yes?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Excuse me, according to this photograph, I cannot show you where the house was because this is not the photograph from the time when I was there, so I cannot show it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you show us where the white house is on this photograph? Is the white house on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No. But the houses along this road have gardens, is that right? They are set back from the road?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There are hedges along the road that border between the houses and the road?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: There is a ditch and there is water in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There are hedges as well, are there not, witness?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: But I now see the hedge otherwise .....

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There was a hedge when you were on guard duty in 1992, was there not, along this road in front of the houses?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I cannot recall if there was a wire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you think that the hedge has perhaps grown since you were on duty there?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I cannot tell you anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There are trees in the gardens of the houses, is that right?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you were at guard post 4, what was between you and the white house? Were there any other buildings?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: From my post to the white house, it was all clear and one could see clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There was not anything obstructing your view in terms of trees or hedges or other buildings?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The pole that you described as being by this house where people were tied against and shot, was that in front of the white house or at the back or at the side?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: It was next to the front of the house, in front of the house, and it was facing, it was turned towards the road between Kozarac and Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So anyone in the school or in the other buildings such as the store at the camp, would they be able to see this pole?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you were looking out of the windows of the school, presumably, you would be able to see people tied up and being shot in front of the white house, if you were looking?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As you have told us, in October 1992, you estimate some 1500 people were in Trnopolje camp at this time?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know one of the prisoners at the camp called Adil Jakupovic?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know his wife Nasiha Jakupovic?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You say that when you were at guard post 4 you were able to see killings in daylight committed by some of the guards in front of that white house, do you?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you have a regular shift that you were on duty for?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What shift was that?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: First shift from morning until the evening, from 7.00 to 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So you were on duty during the hours of the daylight or whatever daylight there was?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is right, is it not, that there was no electricity at this time in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were the telephones working?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What were the names of the other guards who were on your shift duty, 7.00 till 7.00?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, the witness appears to be reluctant to respond to this question. I hear no objection. Sir, you should respond to that question. What are the names of the other guards who were on duty on your shift at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Niemann, why don't you have an objection because my family could be revealed even through other people? I do not want to say.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: There is no objection and the Chamber has entered an order protecting the identity of the family -- prohibiting the eliciting of any information that would identify the family. I do not see how members of the family could be elicited by giving the names of other guards who were on your shift, so you should respond to the question, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, because the Defence can find those who worked in the camp who are around Kozarac, Prijedor, Trnopolje, and through whom one can prove.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You should respond to the question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not want to answer about those names who were guards with me because the Defence could otherwise look for those who are around Kozarac or in Prijedor or Trnopolje, and they could learn from them who my family are and where they are.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Your name has already been given to the Defence -- you realise that -- the name and the position that you held ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: --- in the camp? So if the Defence obtains the names of the guards with whom you work, that appears to be very proper cross-examination because they would then talk with them, presumably, to see whether, in fact, you were working there. You must respond to the question. You must respond to the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They could learn who my family are and where they are. Excuse me, your Honour. I did not give it even to my Court because I had my lawyer who defended me not to give other names.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, you want the names?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I do, your Honour, as it is an important part of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, in order to attempt to assist the Court, may it help if a representative of the Prosecution team spoke to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is a good suggestion. Of course, this witness has revealed the names of other guards at the camp, other guards who, you have indicated, committed offences. So the names of other guards with whom you had contact, you have already offered, you understand that, and we have their names. The Defence has their names. I would suggest that you do talk with the witness. I would ask you to point out to the witness Rule 77(A) of the Rules which provides that the Trial Chamber may hold a witness in contempt of court. If we find that the witness refuses or fails contumaciously to answer a question relevant to the issue before a Chamber, and if we do hold the witness in contempt, the Chamber may impose a fine not exceeding US$10,000 or a term of imprisonment not exceeding six months. It appears that the questions are relevant and you should respond to that question. Keep in mind that these proceedings are closed. Before a transcript of these proceedings is released to the public, the parties will have an opportunity to read the transcript and excise any matter they do not want to be revealed to the public. Also, the Victims and Witnesses Unit may review the transcript for that purpose. But we consider that the question is relevant and you should respond to it. We will stand in recess for five minutes for you to talk to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have spoken with the witness and gone over the various aspects of the matter with him. He is still reluctant to answer the question as such. I have drawn his attention to the provisions of our Rules, Rule 77. What he has agreed to do (and I raise it for consideration) is that if the names are given to him and the Defence have them, he is prepared to indicate on the paper the names of those guards that were at the camp and to put a number beside each guard's name that appears there. But, so far I have been unable to persuade him to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, you have a list of guards' names?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, I do not, your Honour. I am asking the question because I want to find out the information. I am relying on the witness to provide this information. There are certain names that are known through the statements, but what I am asking for here is the shift that he was on and the list of those names. My next question was going to be the names in relation to the other shift from whom they took over. Then I was going to ask him with whom he was on duty at guard post 4, if he was on duty there and where the other guards were positioned.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Defence have been given a copy of a statement of 17th January 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, there are some names in there, but Mr. Kay has indicated that he is going to go further than that, so even that will not be sufficient, and so we still have the other problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We still have a problem, your Honour. I might just say, your Honour, the concern the witness has is that some of these people he knows very well and they came from the same town as he knows, where he lived. The difficulty he has is the moment he mentions them, they will be able to indicate where his family live at the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: And that is not true with the names of the persons he has mentioned already?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour, or that is what he informs, your Honour. The names of the people he has mentioned so far do not fall into that category.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I wonder if you can clarify something for us?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Is it the intention of the Defence, if you are supplied with names of this shift and perhaps other shifts of guards, then to make enquiries to locate those particular guards and communicate with them for one purpose or another? Would that be part of the intention?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It would be, your Honour. We are mindful of paragraph 10 of the order which we have been considering because we have our next trip to Bosnia, as the Court knows, on Saturday. We do not want to go about our business putting anyone at risk or anything like that, but we were mindful for the purposes of investigating the witness adequately that we were able to use information as part of our discovery. I will be frank with the Court. That was very much in mind and what we would set out to do next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Paragraph 10 of the November decision, Mr. Kay, says: "The accused, the defence counsel and their representatives who are acting pursuant to their instructions or requests shall not disclose the name of witness L, or any other identifying data they may discover concerning L, to the public or to the media, except to the limited extent such disclosure to members of the public is necessary to investigate the witness adequately". So, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I mean, I do not want to put these people at risk and we have been talking about this over the last week as we have made our preparations. We considered this wording very carefully, but it was something that we were mindful that we were able to do and we were able to give the name to our interpreters who are acting as agents on our behalf to enable the translations to be given to us. But it is something we do not see that we can stop ourselves from doing in the proper discharge of our duties. If it was not of great importance, I would steer clear and avoid it, but ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I guess my specific question is that you would interpret "except to the limited extent such disclosure to members of the public is necessary to investigate the witness adequately", you would interpret that last phrase as authorising you to disclose the witness's name and the information that you have received from the witness to the guards who he testifies, if he testifies, worked with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Exactly, to investigate his account.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK, that is my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The reason why most of it is being done at this stage is we were conscious we had not got full information and details from this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We had indicated that we would go until 6 o'clock tonight, but in light of the developments the Trial Chamber considers it may be more appropriate to adjourn now to give you more time to talk with witness L. You can tell witness L that it is the decision of the Trial Chamber that this is a question which should be responded to, that it fits within the issues, that it is relevant to the issue before a Chamber and that the Chamber is considering very seriously citing the witness for contempt. Then, of course, we would set a hearing to determine, I suppose, the appropriate penalty for the contempt consistent with the Rule, but that there may be other ramifications too in terms of the receipt of the testimony. So he needs to think about it very carefully. The Chamber would enter an order prohibiting the parties from in any way contacting his relatives, members of his family, in any way intimidating them. That is an order that could be entered by the Chamber which should give him some solace. Other than that, there is nothing that we can do. He needs to understand that when he gives testimony, the Defence should have an opportunity to question his testimony and to test it, and that he cannot simply come and give one side and then expect that they should not have the opportunity to test the validity, the credibility ----

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: --- the truthfulness of his testimony. So we will adjourn until tomorrow at 10 a.m. and then we will see where we are with this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If your Honour pleases.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Just one moment. I just to love to work late hours. This is when I get started -- not in the morning though! So we will hear from L, hopefully, in the morning. We had indicated that we would like to talk with the parties regarding the Defence motion for protective measures, so can we go forward with that, Mr. Wladimiroff and Mr. Niemann? Can we do that at this point?

procedural_notes.text: (The Court adjourned until the following day at 10.00 a.m.)
